rules.title: Berkeley ban on coordinated pricing algorithms for rents and occupancy
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use, and vendors may not sell or provide, coordinated pricing algorithms that use nonpublic competitor data to set or recommend rents or occupancy levels for Berkeley residential units. The City Attorney or an aggrieved tenant can sue, with civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation.
rules.key_value: ban on coordinated pricing algorithms using nonpublic competitor data (<90 days old); civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley
rules.effective_date_note: The ordinance text provided (D001) states no effective date; 2026-03-01 is the date reported for the ordinance in the challenge context. The law-firm alert (D002/D037) says January 2026.
rules.exemptions: Excludes aggregated anonymous reports that do not recommend rents, affordable-housing rent/income limit products, and market research for financing, appraisal, or software development research/testing/training.
rules.penalty: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; damages, injunctive relief, restitution; each month and each unit is a separate violation; prevailing plaintiff gets attorney's fees
rules.conflict_note: Two published effective dates: March 1, 2026 (ordinance text per reports) vs. January 2026 (Morgan Lewis alert, D002/D037). The provided ordinance copy does not state a date.

rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Berkeley landlords may not ask about or use criminal history in advertising, applications, tenant selection, or lease decisions, and must give written notice and a chance to respond before taking any action based on criminal history.
rules.key_value: ban on criminal-history inquiries and use in tenant selection
citation_aliases: Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making
rules.effective_date_note: Council passed the ordinance April 14, 2020; the document does not state the effective date.
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties; owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner of record lives in one unit; units rented under an agreement allowing owners to move back (BMC 13.76.130 A.9); existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.
rules.penalty: Administrative fines of $1,000 to $10,000 per violation, actual damages or three times one month's rent, punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, and injunctive relief.

unverifiable_exemptions: existing tenants subletting or adding/replacing roommates

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Good Cause Ordinance – just cause, notices and relocation assistance
rules.requirement: Tenants in fully or partially covered units can be evicted only for just cause. A landlord cannot evict for nonpayment unless rent owed is at least one month of HUD Fair Market Rent, cannot evict for refusing to sign a new fixed-term lease, must describe lease breaches and harm in detail, and must file termination notices with the Rent Board within three business days. Owner move-in and Ellis Act evictions require relocation payments (2026: $19,413 plus $6,471 for qualifying households).
rules.key_value: Just cause required; nonpayment eviction only if debt ≥ 1 month HUD FMR; OMI/Ellis relocation $19,413 + $6,471 (2026)
rules.quoted_span: For a landlord to evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent, the tenant must owe an amount of rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent (FMR) value
rules.effective_date_note: Measure BB passed November 2024; no general effective date stated. Relocation amounts adjusted effective 2026-01-01 (approved by Rent Board 2025-10-16).
rules.exemptions: Exempt: golden duplexes, owner-shared kitchen/bath units where owner lived there first, certain ADU properties, university housing and nonprofit cooperatives.
rules.review_note: Chapter number 13.76 inferred from other Berkeley documents (D008, D003); D006 and D004 do not state it.

unverifiable_exemptions: unit shared with landlord who lived there first

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Stabilization Ordinance – Annual General Adjustment (max 5%)
rules.requirement: For fully covered (mostly pre-1980 multifamily) units, yearly rent increases are limited to the Annual General Adjustment set by the Rent Board (65% of CPI, never above 5%). The 2026 AGA is 1.0%; banked unused AGAs can still be used to reach the rent ceiling.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%
rules.effective_date_note: Measure BB cap passed November 2024; no effective date stated. 2026 AGA effective no earlier than 2026-01-01.
rules.exemptions: Partially covered and exempt units (new construction with CO after June 1980, most single-family homes and condos) have no rent ceiling; 2026 AGA does not adjust tenancies begun on or after 2025-01-01 with rents set under Costa-Hawkins.
rules.interaction: Local rent control governs instead of the state Tenant Protection Act cap for covered units; state Costa-Hawkins limits local control on newer buildings and single-family homes/condos.
rules.conflict_note: Documents give the cutoff as 'built before 1980' (D006, D009 table) and 'CO after June 1980' for new construction (D009); the exact boundary is ambiguous, June 30, 1980 used.

unverifiable_exemptions: single-family homes with tenancies begun before 1996

rules.title: Berkeley security deposit interest requirement
rules.requirement: For units fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on security deposits at the end of each year, prorated if the tenant moves out earlier. The deposit cap itself comes from state law.
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year
rules.coverage_conditions: Units fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.
rules.interaction: Operates alongside state cap in Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5.
rules.review_note: Section number not stated in documents; ch. 13.76 inferred as the Rent Ordinance chapter.

rules.title: Berkeley tenant screening fee disclosure and ban on renewal fees (ch. 13.78)
rules.requirement: Owners who charge a screening fee must disclose, before taking the fee, a Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement and the maximum fee cap under Civ. Code 1950.6(b) (2026: $68.96). Landlords also cannot charge existing tenants non-refundable fees to renew a tenancy or to add or replace a roommate.
rules.key_value: Disclosure of fee rights and cap before collecting fee; no non-refundable renewal/roommate fees
rules.quoted_span: the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under

parsed.notes: Berkeley: merged three algorithmic-ban candidates (ch. 13.63); merged just-cause/relocation, rent control/AGA, deposit-interest, and ch. 13.78 fee candidates into one record per law. The ch. 13.63 effective date is disputed (March 2026 vs January 2026). The rent-control cutoff is ambiguous (before 1980 vs CO after June 1980).
